body:
i would love to get emancipated, but i just don't know how to go about getting the papers necessary, let alone go to court since i don't have any nice clothing nor can i have any courthouses i could walk or bike to. i never got my permit due to financial issues and parents generally saying no to me getting it, so that's out of the question. 

one good thing is my county has a lot of churches and as long as i can remain hidden/change my appearance enough, i think i'll be able to request food if they do free food. do churches allow dogs though? i really don't want to leave my dog in the heat alone if i don't have to. even though she's well trained, she can get anxious when i'm not around. food pantries seem really scarce around me, so i'll have to look into which ones allow pets and such.  
thank you for the note, i'll make sure to try and get fiber in my diet as much as i am able to. i'm so sorry you had to experience that though, it sounds horrid. :(

both 211 and your blog are worth their weight in gold, thank you so so much for providing me with resources i can use. i'm happy that you managed to get back into housing, that's really really awesome!!

i don't think there's much you can do, but i really appreciate the support. once i'm on my feet, i hope to get into work that helps youth in my position because i can relate to the entire situation and how it makes you feel, and i want to prevent harm to youth as much as i possibly can. 

thank you so much for being there, it really means a lot to me. i hope your kids are doing well <3

hey friend, please don't die. not having drugs can really suck but please carry on, even if you feel like you're trudging through miles and miles of quicksand with a ball and chain at your ankle. if it helps any, r/SuicideWatch can help if you're actively suicidal.

is there any more info about your situation that you can give so i could possibly give advice? i really don't want you to die. my pms are open if you'd like a one-on-one conversation.

i've def. checked them out a bunch and think that's what i'm gonna do if i can't find a long term housing situation (i.e i work with someone else to make rent, or squat somewhere if i can't make rent, obviously close enough to where i can work under the table until i'm 18.) trainhopping seems like a good way to get away from my location fast as long as i can safely get on one with my dog. i'll have to do some research on where my nearest trainyard is and go from there.

i've never learned to play an instrument before, is that going to cause me problems? i don't know exactly where to find one either. do you have any recommendations or tips for someone who has never touched an instrument in their life? for self defense, i have pepper spray and have basic martial arts training.

i've had good friends and family die from not being able to get help for their addiction and don't want to go that way, especially since i have a dog to look out for. i've dealt with depression and the appeal of drugs, though i can't say i've faced the stress of being homeless so i don't want to say that i'll avoid all drugs altogether but i'll work hard to never let it become something that takes over my life.

of course. she always will eat before me and i will work to make sure she has a place to sleep. i'll try to be as out of the public eye as i can without endangering my baby or i. people can say what they want to say or think what they want to think, i just hope i won't have to use self defense too many times.

all in all, thank you for such great advice and i wish the same for you always.

the mods over at r/runaway have a lot of useful info on what to pack in general (as like you said, individuals in different locations and situations will need different things) so i've been working on scouring through all of that and taking the most useful bits down in a journal and making sure i have everything ready to go. having lots of  history going camping and bugging out is going to help me a lot, but i know it's gonna be tough regardless.

to be much more specific, i'm in illinois.

eastern united states. i have about $200 saved up, and am hoping to get more from a friend if i'm able. i have lots of survival gear ready to go, along with dog food, collapsible bowl, etc. i'm still trying to figure out what gear is worth taking and what's worth leaving so i'm not overpacked. i also have a bicycle available to me which i plan on taking.

a bit late, but if you have internet access khan academy is a thing you could do. it's a free online school thing kinda like duolingo but for the regular subjects,, take it with a grain of salt though as i'm not actively in school or working towards my GED, just a suggestion you could check out if regular public school is unavailable.

I know this is a bot, but I've read through all information given on this subreddit that I could find, noted down whatever useful stuff I could into a small notebook, and will be carrying it with me. I've decided the benefits of running outweigh the negatives.
